faq.q: Do I need a demolition permit?
faq.a: Often, yes. Within an area covered by a detailed development plan, a demolition permit is normally required to demolish a building or part of one, and outside such areas a demolition notification may be required. The municipal building committee decides. We prepare the documents and handle contact with the municipality.

faq.q: How long does demolition take?
faq.a: It depends on size, materials and whether remediation is needed. A bathroom often takes a few days, a whole building longer. The quote includes a schedule.

faq.q: Can I use the ROT tax deduction?
faq.a: Demolition that is part of renovating your home, for example before a new bathroom or kitchen, may qualify for the ROT deduction on labour costs. Demolishing an entire building normally does not. Check the current rules with the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket) – we itemise the labour cost on the invoice.

faq.q: What happens to the demolition material?
faq.a: We sort it on site into separate fractions and take it to approved facilities. Anything that can be reused is salvaged. You get documentation of what was delivered and where.

faq.q: How is asbestos handled?
faq.a: If the survey finds asbestos, it is removed before demolition starts, by trained staff following the Swedish Work Environment Authority’s regulations. Read more on the remediation page.

faq.q: How is asbestos handled?
faq.a: Asbestos is removed before any other work starts. The area is enclosed and put under negative pressure, staff use respiratory protection and protective clothing, and the waste is packaged and taken to an approved facility. The work follows the Swedish Work Environment Authority’s regulations, which require special training and in some cases a permit.

faq.q: How do I know if my building contains asbestos or PCB?
faq.a: The construction year gives an indication: asbestos mainly occurs in buildings built or renovated before 1982, PCB in buildings built or renovated 1956–1973. A survey with sampling gives a definite answer.

faq.q: Who is responsible for surveying hazardous materials?
faq.a: The developer – usually the property owner – is responsible for identifying hazardous materials before demolition. We can carry out the survey for you.

faq.q: Do I have to move out during remediation?
faq.a: It depends on where and how much needs to be remediated. You can often stay if the work area is sealed off. We go through this at the site visit.

faq.q: Can I use the ROT tax deduction?
faq.a: Remediation done as part of renovating your home may in some cases qualify for the ROT deduction on labour costs. The rules change from time to time, so check with the Swedish Tax Agency. We itemise the labour cost on the invoice.

faq.q: Do I need a permit or notification for a new opening?
faq.a: Work on a load-bearing structure normally requires a notification to the municipality and documentation from a structural engineer. In a housing cooperative apartment you also need the board’s permission. We help you work out what applies.

faq.q: Will there be a lot of dust?
faq.a: We usually saw and drill with water, which binds the dust. We protect surrounding surfaces and collect the water.

faq.q: Can you cut openings in a cooperative apartment?
faq.a: Yes. We coordinate with the association, plan the work to disturb neighbours as little as possible and keep to the association’s working hours.

faq.q: What is the difference between design-build and build-only?
faq.a: In design-build we are responsible for both design and construction. In build-only we build according to documents that you as the client have produced. Which suits you depends on how far you have come in planning.

faq.q: Can you demolish the old house and build a new one?
faq.a: Yes. Demolition, remediation and new construction in one project, with one contact person, is exactly what we are here for.

faq.q: Can I use the ROT deduction for new construction?
faq.a: No, the ROT deduction does not apply to new construction. It may apply to extending an existing home. Check the current rules with the Swedish Tax Agency.

faq.q: Who applies for the building permit?
faq.a: As the developer, you are responsible for having a permit. In a design-build contract we can produce the documents and handle the application for you.

faq.q: Do I need a building permit for a loft conversion?
faq.a: A loft conversion may require a building permit or notification, especially if you change the facade, add roof windows or alter load-bearing structures. Check with the municipality – we help with the documents.

faq.q: Can you work while our business is operating?

faq.q: Can I use the ROT tax deduction?

faq.q: What does pipe replacement preparation include?

faq.q: Can I put the container on the street?
faq.a: On your own property, no permit is normally needed. If the container will stand on a street, pavement or other public place, a permit from the police or the municipality is usually required. We help you with the application.

faq.q: What must not go in the container?
faq.a: Hazardous waste such as paint, chemicals, electronics, asbestos and pressure-treated wood must be kept separate. Ask us if you are unsure.

faq.q: Why does construction waste have to be sorted?
faq.a: Under the Swedish Waste Ordinance, construction and demolition waste must be sorted into several fractions, including wood, mineral, metal, glass, plastic and plaster. This means more can be recycled, and sorted waste is often cheaper to deliver.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This describes how {company} processes personal data when you contact us, request a quote or apply for a job. The template must be reviewed and completed before publication.

p: {company}, corporate ID no. {orgnr}, {address}, is the data controller. Questions about personal data can be sent to {email}.
We process the data you provide to us:
list: Quote requests: name, company/housing association, email, phone, property address, description of the job and any photos and drawings you attach.
Job applications: name, contact details, CV and the information you write in your application.
Contact by email and phone: the information included in the contact.
Answering requests and providing quotes – steps prior to entering a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
Carrying out jobs and contracts – contract (Art. 6(1)(b)).
Bookkeeping and invoicing – legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)), Swedish Bookkeeping Act.
Recruitment – consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you give when you submit your application.
Quote requests that do not lead to a job are deleted when they are no longer needed to answer the request.
Job applications are deleted when the recruitment has ended, unless you consent to us keeping them longer.
Accounting records: seven years under the Swedish Bookkeeping Act.

p: We never sell your data. We use suppliers that process data on our behalf:
list: A form service that receives what you send through the website’s forms.
A web host that runs the website.
An email service we use to reply to you.

p: You have the right to request access to, rectification or erasure of your data, restriction of processing, to object to processing and to receive your data (data portability). If you have given consent, you can withdraw it at any time. Contact us at {email}.
You have the right to lodge a complaint with the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY), imy.se.
Read about how we use cookies on the Cookies page.

meta.title: Cookies
meta.description: Information about cookies and website analytics on our website.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: A cookie is a small text file stored in your browser. Under the Swedish Electronic Communications Act, you must be informed about which cookies are used and consent to those that are not strictly necessary.
cookies.none: This website does not set any cookies. We use no tracking and do not embed maps or social feeds. The map on the contact page is an image – Google Maps only opens when you click the link.
cookies.session: The quote form stores what you have entered in your browser’s session storage (not a cookie) so you can move back and forth between steps. The data is deleted when you close the tab or submit the form.
cookies.analyticsOn: If you agree, we use website analytics from {provider} to see how the pages are used. Analytics only load after your consent and can be switched off at any time.
cookies.manage: You can also delete stored data in your browser settings.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.intro: {company} is responsible for this website. We want as many people as possible to be able to use it.

p: The website is built to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, visible focus, sufficient contrast, text alternatives and screen reader support.
Found something that doesn’t work? Contact us at {email} and we’ll fix it.
The website has been tested with the automated tools Lighthouse and axe.

consent.text: We would like to use website analytics to improve the site. Nothing loads without your consent.
